title: The Riverbank

headings.text: How the new fish pass works

key_sentences: Camera traps have recorded a family of otters on the upper river for the first time in more than twenty years.
The footage was captured in late August by one of the six cameras that volunteers installed along the mill race last spring.
Their return is a sign that the water quality improvements of the past decade are working.
The fish pass at Hollins Weir has allowed trout to move upstream again, giving otters a reliable food supply.
Phosphate at Corley Farm has halved since the reed beds were planted, while the reading below the sewage works remains the weakest on the river.
This summer our volunteers gave more than 1,400 hours to the river.
Working parties meet on the second Saturday of each month.
A counter at the top pool recorded 2,300 trout and 41 salmon between April and September.
Members receive this newsletter four times a year and can vote at the annual general meeting.

list_items.text: How the new fish pass works
12 Oct – Balsam pull at Corley Farm, 10 am
26 Oct – Annual general meeting, Millbrook Village Hall, 7 pm
7 Dec – Winter walk to the weir, meet at the church
Fish swimming upstream are drawn to the strong flow at the bottom of the pass.
They move up a series of pools, each about twenty centimetres higher than the last.
Slots between the pools let them rest before the next jump.
At the top they rejoin the river above the weir.
